Given a query q and document d, fQ encodes q into a bag of ﬁxed-size embeddings Eq while fD en- codes d into another bag Ed. Crucially, each embeddings in Eq and Ed is contextualized based on the other terms in q or d, respectively. We describe our BERT-based encoders in §3.2. Using Eq and Ed, ColBERT computes the relevance score be- tween q and d via late interaction, which we deﬁne as a summation of maximum similarity (MaxSim) operators.

Title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
As illustrated, every query embedding interacts with all document embeddings via a MaxSim operator, which computes maximum similarity (e.g., cosine similarity), and the scalar outputs of these operators are summed across query terms. Tis paradigm allows ColBERT to exploit deep LM-based representations while shifing the cost of encoding documents of- ﬂine and amortizing the cost of encoding the query once across all ranked documents.
